title: When the Yearbook Breaks
premise: Silas Thackeray, a senior coder who runs an anonymous gossip account about her small town's elite academy, counts the days to graduation while hiding from a family legacy she wants no part of. When the school's beloved yearbook tradition faces shutdown after decades of archives mysteriously vanish, the teacher pairs Silas with her nemesis, golden-boy editor Theo Vance, to rebuild it. Digging through old yearbooks, they uncover that Silas's anonymous account has been leaking secrets someone planted long ago—and that Theo's family helped bury them. As graduation looms, Silas must choose between exposing the truth and protecting the found family of misfits who've become her real home, ending with her publishing everything under her own name and saving the yearbook as a living archive instead of a shrine.
about_author: Casper Fairweather is the pen name of a former school archivist who spent years cataloguing other people's memories before writing her own. She lives in a coastal town much like Millbrook, where the yearbook club still meets on Thursdays.

chapters.title: Ninety-Seven Days
chapters.summary: Silas's POV. Opening day of senior semester; she posts anonymously about classmates' secrets, counting down to escape from Millbrook Academy and her overbearing grandmother's expectations. Emotional beat: restless detachment masking loneliness.

chapters.title: The Assignment
chapters.summary: Silas's POV. Ms. Okafor announces the yearbook restoration project and pairs Silas with Theo Vance, her longtime rival, after the archive room flood destroys decades of records. Beat: dread and indignation.

chapters.title: Enemy Territory
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. He resents being paired with the girl whose anonymous account once humiliated his best friend, but notices Silas's genuine skill restoring damaged photographs. Beat: grudging curiosity.

chapters.title: Water Damage
chapters.summary: Silas's POV. Sorting soaked yearbooks, they find 1987's volume missing entirely—razored out of every copy in the archive. First hint of deliberate erasure. Beat: unease beneath sarcasm.

chapters.title: The Misfit Table
chapters.summary: Silas's POV. Lunch with her found family—Priya, Dez, and quiet Marisol—who tease her about spending time with Theo. We learn why each of them needs the yearbook tradition. Beat: warmth and belonging.

chapters.title: Anonymous Noises
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. He starts suspecting the gossip account's source of information is impossibly precise, almost like someone reading old records. Beat: suspicion sharpening into investigation.

chapters.title: Grandmother's Attic
chapters.summary: Silas's POV. Sent to fetch family heirlooms, Silas finds her late mother's yearbooks—1987 among them—with pages torn out and a photo of young Theo's father circled. Beat: shaken discovery.

chapters.title: Truce Terms
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Working late in the archive, Silas and Theo strike an uneasy deal: share what they find, trust no one else. A near-moment of connection interrupted by a security guard. Beat: fragile alliance.

chapters.title: What Priya Knew
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. She reveals her scholarship depends on the school's image, explaining why administrators might want certain histories gone. Beat: loyalty tested by fear.

chapters.title: The Founder's Daughter
chapters.summary: Silas's POV. Her grandmother Thackeray was class of '87; the family name is on the archive wing itself. Silas realizes the vanished yearbook may implicate her own bloodline. Beat: identity crisis.

chapters.title: Fire Drill
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Someone ransacks their workroom the night they photograph the torn pages; only the cloud backup saves them. They realize the account's leaks are being used to flush out whoever remembers '87. Beat: fear turning to resolve.

chapters.title: Marisol Speaks
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV. The quietest friend confesses her older sister was expelled years ago after a story broke—an early post from Silas's account she never knew the origin of. Beat: guilt crashing over Silas.

chapters.title: Reconstruction
chapters.summary: Silas's POV. Using code to digitally reassemble the razored pages from fragments, Silas and Theo work through the night and recover one full spread: a hazing incident covered up by founding families—including both theirs. Beat: grim clarity.

chapters.title: Duty Calls
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. His father offers him early admission and a future in exchange for dropping the project quietly. Theo sees, for the first time, how love in his house is transactional. Beat: heartbreak and defiance.

chapters.title: The Account Exposed
chapters.summary: Silas's POV. An anonymous tip outs Silas as the gossip account's author to the whole school. Friends reel; Theo stands beside her publicly anyway. Beat: public shame, unexpected solidarity.

chapters.title: Seventeen Days
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. With graduation near and the administration moving to cancel the yearbook permanently, the group races to finish the restored volume as evidence and tribute. Beat: ticking-clock urgency.

chapters.title: Grandmother's Confession
chapters.summary: Silas's POV. Her grandmother admits she helped bury the '87 incident to protect the family name, believing silence was love. Silas rejects the inheritance of secrecy. Beat: generational rupture and release.

chapters.title: Deadline
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. The board votes to shutter the archive; Theo burns his father's offer in front of the assembly by requesting the floor. Beat: courage against duty.

chapters.title: Publish It All
chapters.summary: Silas's POV. Instead of another anonymous drop, Silas posts the reconstructed truth under her real name, taking responsibility for every past post, including the ones that hurt Marisol. Beat: accountability as redemption.

chapters.title: The Vote
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs. Students, alumni, and the expelled sister testify; the board reverses course, making the yearbook a permanent student-run living archive. Beat: collective triumph.

chapters.title: Signing Day
chapters.summary: Silas's POV. Graduation. The first page of the new yearbook is blank except for signatures—hers, Theo's, and her friends'. She and Theo admit what's grown between them. Beat: tender resolution.

chapters.title: Day One
chapters.summary: Epilogue, Silas's POV. Summer begins; the countdown habit breaks at last. Silas archives the old account forever and opens a new notebook titled with tomorrow's date. Beat: hope without escape.
